contributions.headingText: Salivary gland carcinoma NOS represents a heterogeneous spectrum of carcinomas forming epithelial, ductal, and/or glandular structures, and it is a diagnosis of exclusion, specifically of otherwise-defined salivary gland carcinoma entities.

8140/3 Adenocarcinoma, NOS

8290/3 Oncocytic adenocarcinoma

8144/3 Intestinal-type adenocarcinoma

2B67.Z Malignant neoplasms of parotid gland, unspecified

2B68.Z Malignant neoplasms of submandibular or sublingual glands, unspecified

2B60.Z Malignant neoplasms of lip, unspecified

2B65.Z Malignant neoplasms of palate, unspecified

2B66.Z Malignant neoplasms of other or unspecified parts of mouth, unspecified
Not recommended: unclassified adenocarcinoma; ductal adenocarcinoma; (papillary) cystadenocarcinoma.
More than 50% of cases arise in the parotid gland {7125074; 8944036; 21612974}, and 40% arise in minor glands, most often in the hard palate, buccal mucosa, and lips {8944036; 17577550}.

Patients with tumours of major glands usually present with asymptomatic, solitary, firm or cystic masses. Occasionally, they may be painful. Tumours in the palate often ulcerate and may erode bony structures {7125074}.

Because of morphogenetic identification of new types of salivary gland adenocarcinoma {27233253; 31094920}, the entity adenocarcinoma NOS now accounts for only 5–10% of salivary gland carcinomas {7125074; 21612974}. The average patient age is 58 years, with a wide age range {12167424; 21612974}. They are extremely rare in children.
Tumours may be partly circumscribed but usually have an irregular and infiltrative appearance. The cut surface is commonly tan or yellow, sometimes with areas of necrosis and haemorrhage.

Tumours display a wide range of ductal or glandular proliferation patterns, with or without a cystic component or necrosis. There is a variety of architectural growth patterns, including small confluent nests or cords, large islands, and (often) associated densely cellular stroma. Tumour cells can be cuboidal, columnar, polygonal, clear, mucinous, oncocytoid, or plasmacytoid. Ductal and glandular structures are predominant in low- and intermediate-grade tumours, but less frequent in high-grade tumours {15578883; 16673121}.

Proof of an intraductal component supports a salivary gland origin {16673121}.

Subtypes

These include oncocytic adenocarcinoma {8944036; 20738418} and intestinal-type {19695679; 21948243; 23108630} adenocarcinoma, the latter of which is often positive for CK20 and CDX2.

Immunohistochemistry

Immunohistochemistry is helpful in distinguishing adenocarcinoma NOS from acinic cell carcinoma (NR4A3, DOG1) {12608654}, tumours with myoepithelial/basal cell composition (calponin, CK5/6, p63), and metastatic adenocarcinoma (site-specific markers) {14976534}.

Differential diagnosis

For the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma NOS to be rendered, other primary carcinoma types must be excluded, including salivary duct carcinoma, mucoepidermoid carcinoma, polymorphous adenocarcinoma, and high-grade transformation of other types of salivary carcinoma {14976534}. Tumours with significant mucinous differentiation may be better regarded as mucinous adenocarcinoma.

Smears show adenocarcinoma with (usually) high-grade nuclei in a necrotic background, and they lack the features of other salivary gland carcinomas, resulting in a differential diagnosis of metastases from colon and lung. Oncocytic and intestinal types are recognized {7125074}.
Molecular alterations are heterogeneous and not diagnostic {27334835}.
Essential: a salivary gland carcinoma lacking the morphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular features of other salivary carcinomas; exclusion of metastasis is mandatory.
Staging follows the eighth edition of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) / American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) TNM staging system.

Prognosis is influenced by location, histological grade, and clinical stage {7125074; 27166875}. High-grade adenocarcinoma NOS is an aggressive malignancy. A study showed 15-year survival rates of 54%, 31%, and 3% for low-, intermediate-, and high-grade tumours, respectively {7125074}. The survival rate for adenocarcinoma with a significant cystic component is more favourable {8944036}. The reports of intestinal-type adenocarcinoma suggest an aggressive behaviour {19695679; 23108630}.
